topics.label: Lecture framing and the cancer hallmarks framework
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture's learning outcomes and introduces the hallmarks framework used to explain cancer's loss of growth control.

topics.label: Mutational deregulation of growth and survival signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signalling pathways make cancer cells proliferate and survive independently of normal growth controls.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation sustains abnormal cell populations, using blood cancers and intestinal epithelial renewal as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered p53 signalling and the balance of apoptotic regulators allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and cancer cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how cancer cells overcome it by reactivating telomerase.

topics.label: Genome safeguards and mutation-driven loss of growth control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of mutation-driven loss of growth control by explaining p53's genome-protective responses before recapping how mutations produce cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and participates in self-reinforcing changes to gene regulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis supporting tumour growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumours activate blood vessel formation to obtain the oxygen and nutrients needed for continued growth.

topics.label: Metastatic spread and survival at secondary sites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells disseminate and establish secondary tumours, emphasizing the difficulty of identifying a distinct genetic basis for metastatic success.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's learning goals, summarizes convergence on shared cancer hallmarks, and offers further reading before inviting questions.
